Set Control Parameters for Simulation

Source: R/parameter_estimation.R
set_control_mcmc.Rd

This function sets control parameters for running simulations, supporting MCMC methods for glgpm models.

Usage

set_control_mcmc(
  n_sim = 22000,
  burnin = 2000,
  thin = 10,
  h = NULL,
  c1.h = 1,
  c2.h = 0.6,
  linear_model = FALSE
)

Arguments

n_sim

Integer. The total number of simulations to run. Default is 22000, which with the default burn-in and thinning keeps 2,000 draws. With linear_model = TRUE it is the number of independent draws, 2,000 by default.

burnin

Integer. The number of initial simulations to discard (burn-in/warmup period). Default is 2000.

thin

Integer. The interval at which simulations are recorded (thinning interval, MCMC only). Default is 10.

h

Numeric. An optional positive step size for Langevin MCMC.

c1.h

Numeric. Positive scale for the burn-in Robbins-Monro step-size adaptation. Default is 1.

c2.h

Numeric. Exponent controlling the diminishing adaptation gain. Must be larger than 0.5 and no larger than 1. Default is 0.6.

linear_model

Logical. If TRUE, sets up parameters for a linear model. Default is FALSE.

Value

A list of control parameters with class "RiskMap_control_mcmc". Contents depend on sampler:

  • For "mcmc": n_sim, burnin, thin, h, c1.h, c2.h, linear_model

Details

If linear_model = TRUE, only n_sim is required.

During burn-in the step size of the Langevin chain is adapted towards an acceptance rate of 0.574, starting from h (by default \(1.65 / d^{1/6}\) for \(d\) latent effects). The step kept after burn-in is the geometric mean of the adapted step over the second half of burn-in.

Seeds are not part of the control settings. Pass seed to glgpm(), predict.RiskMap(), assess_prediction() or assess_simulation().

See also

glgpm

Examples

# Default parameters (MCMC)
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc()

# Custom MCMC parameters
control_mcmc <- set_control_mcmc(n_sim = 15000, burnin = 3000, thin = 20)
